Handmade Passover Matzah

Served at: Passover

6-8 small matzahsPrep 10 min (total process must be under 18 min)Cook 3-5 min per matzah

Matzah is the unleavened bread central to the Passover Seder, symbolizing the haste with which the Israelites left Egypt, without time for their bread to rise. Its simple ingredients and quick preparation are a direct reflection of this ancient story, making it a powerful and symbolic food during the holiday.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (120 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) cold water
  • Pinch of salt (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 500°F (260°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment paper or leave them ungreased. Have all your tools ready: a large bowl, measuring cups, a rolling pin, and a fork or matzah perforator.
  2. In the large bowl, combine the flour and salt (if using). Add the cold water all at once and quickly mix with your hands or a wooden spoon until a shaggy dough forms.
  3. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead quickly for no more than 1-2 minutes, just until it comes together into a cohesive ball. Do not over-knead.
  4. Immediately divide the dough into 6-8 equal pieces. Working quickly with one piece at a time, roll it out as thinly as possible (about 1/16 inch or 1.5 mm) into a rough circle or square.
  5. Using a fork or a matzah perforator, prick the entire surface of the rolled-out dough thoroughly and evenly. This prevents it from puffing up like regular bread.
  6. Transfer the perforated dough to the preheated baking sheet. Bake for 3-5 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the matzah is lightly golden brown and crisp. Watch carefully as it burns quickly.
  7. Remove from the oven and let cool completely on a wire rack. Repeat with the remaining dough, ensuring the entire process from water touching flour to the matzah entering the oven is completed within 18 minutes for each batch.

Tips

  • The 18-minute rule is paramount: from the moment water touches flour, the matzah must be in the oven within 18 minutes to be considered kosher for Passover. Work quickly and efficiently.
  • Use cold water to slow down any potential leavening process.
  • Roll the dough as thin as possible for the crispiest matzah. Any thicker and it might be chewy.
